result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A reduces the badges to quiet outline tags, drops the card borders, and gives Starter and Scale outline buttons so the Team solid button stands out. B keeps the loud yellow badges and gives two of the three cards equally loud white buttons. B also puts a uniform-style card edge on all cards, but its yellow badges still compete with the price. A is a bit weaker on baseline alignment because the featured card has different padding, and it says it didn't save or render the file. B's padding change on the featured card has the same effect. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B keeps the price dominant, marks Team with a label plus a larger white card and shadow, and quiets the badges to outlines. It also ranks the buttons, with the one solid button on Team and outlines on the others. A keeps the yellow badges loud and leaves Starter and Scale with equally loud white buttons, so its button ranking is weaker. A also puts the (recommended) label on its own line, and its heading is a small uppercase label. B has a minor flaw: it doesn't add href to the links.
